Headline: The message to send after a ceramic coating

Subhead: What to put in a message after handover, and how to send it from the booking itself.

Reader: Studios applying ceramic coatings who explain the care verbally, if at all, and hear nothing until a car comes back damaged

Facts you may state (and ONLY these):
- Customer profiles carry private notes and a full service history visible only to the studio.
- Service status updates let a studio message a client about a job in progress.

Close with a call to action asking the reader to DM the keyword AFTERCARE.

Do not invent CLAIMS of any kind: no statistics, no facts, no list items the source above does not contain. Compress the given sentences — cut words, never substitute your own. When the source presents a list as ordered, keep its order and do not add or drop items.

Lead with the reader's problem, not with the product.

BRAND VOICE: Quietly confident and aspirational, addressing the studio owner directly with understated elegance — evocative fragments over hype, with a flash of urgency when revenue is on the line.
PHOTOGRAPHY: this brand uses images sparingly, to support the type — ask for one only where it genuinely adds proof or atmosphere.
DO: Speak to 'you', the owner; Short evocative fragments; Concrete numbers and outcomes; Let restraint carry the confidence
DON'T: Exclamation-heavy hype; Generic SaaS jargon; Cramming multiple claims into one line; Overusing the gold accent
HANDLE: detailmasters.pro
SLIDES: exactly 6. Not one more, not one fewer — split or merge your points to land on that number.

  · This brand's body copy is always cut after it is written — aim about 52 characters shorter than the budget allows.
